newsitem.title: USA: Stokely expects to violate debt pacts.
newsitem.headline: Stokely expects to violate debt pacts.

text.p: Stokely USA Inc said Wednesday that by the end of its fiscal second quarter in September it expects to be violation of certain financial covenants contained in its long-term debt agreements.
Stokely, which produces canned and frozen vegetables, said it would seek to obtain waivers.
It said it was in compliance with all debt covenants as of June 30.
Stokely said that despite progress it has made to restructure its business, it is unable to operate profitably under current market conditions.
"We believe the historically low selling prices that currently exist are primarily due to excess inventories," Stephen Theobald, president, said in a statement.
He said the U.S. Agriculture Department reported on July 10 that planted acres of corn and green beans for canned vegetable processors were down 10 percent from a year earlier.

"It is uncertain when reductions of that magnitude might lead to an improved pricing environment; however, we expect continuation of the significant margin pressure that currently exists at least through the second quarter," Theobald said.
Stokely today reported a net loss for the first quarter ended June 30 of $0.24 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.38.
Sales fell to $36.3 million from $42.3 million.
Sales dropped primarily due to an $11.3 million decrease in frozen vegetable sales, partially offset by a $5.3 million, or 17 percent, increase in canned vegetable sales.
